answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: no real or imaginary values of \(t\)

solutions.text:
For the expression to vanish, one would need \[ \sqrt{25-t^2}=-5. \] The radical sign denotes the principal square root. It is nonnegative for a nonnegative real radicand and, over the complex numbers, is chosen with nonnegative real part; it therefore cannot equal \(-5.\) Squaring would introduce the extraneous candidate \(t=0,\) for which the original expression is \(10.\)

Thus, no real or imaginary value works, and the correct answer is A.
hints: Isolate the radical before doing any algebra
If you square, check every candidate in the original equation because the radical has a prescribed sign
